Date of such order 12-07-2024  JUDGMENT The Police Sub-Inspector of Cubbon Park Police Station has filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 420, 465, 468 of IPC.
2. The prosecution case is that:
The accused has applied for a home loan in Bank of Baroda to purchase property bearing house No.1009, 1 st floor, situated at 1st Block, Janapriya Apartment,
Machohalli Village, Dasanapura Hobli, Bengaluru North.
But in the A.G's office where she works, she is getting a salary of Rs.1,195/- p.m. after deducting all deductions, and as she could not get a loan from the bank.

Accordingly, she fabricated and forged salary slip similar to the salary slip given in the AGs office, in which she was paid Rs.14,051/-, by creating a fake salary slip to the bank and availed a sum of Rs.6,45,000/-, thereby accused cheated the bank.
Accordingly, CW1 being Chief Manager of the Bank has lodged first information before the J.C.Nagara Police.
The said police have registered the case.
After investigation, the I.O. filed charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 420, 465, 468 of IPC.
3. The accused is on bail.

After furnishing the prosecution papers in compliance of Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. and on hearing both the sides, this court has framed charges against accused for the alleged offences, read over and explained to her.
She pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

4. To substantiate its case, the prosecution has examined in all eight witnesses as PW.1 to 8 and got marked thirty two documents as per Ex.P.1 to 32.
5.
Thereafter, the accused was examined U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. to enable her to explain the incriminating evidence appeared against her in the evidence of prosecution witnesses.
She denied the same and not chosen to lead any defence evidence.

6. Heard arguments from both sides and perused the material available on record, the points that arise for my determination are:

2 1.

sentences.text:
Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 10-04-2006,
the accused with dishonest intention to have wrongful gain has forged and fabricated salary certificate of AGS office, where she works and used the same for the purpose of cheating and thereby committed the offences punishable U/sec.465, 468 of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after forging the salary slip the accused have availed housing loan for a sum of Rs.6,45,000/- from the Bank of Baroda, situated at M.G. Road and cheated the Bank and thereby committed the offence punishable U/sec.420 of IPC?
3. What order?
7. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the Negative  Point No.2 : In the Negative  Point No.3 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 8. Point No.1 and 2: In order to avoid repetition of facts and discussion, I have taken both these points together for common consideration for the sake of brevity.

9. In order to prove the case, the prosecution has examined first informant CW1 Sambhudayal Sharma, Bank officials CW2 J.B.Maskarenus, CW4 Venkata Ramanarao, CW5 Lalitha, CW7 Srirama Murthy, CW8 Selvaraj, police officials CW10 Shivaswamy and CW11 Roopa Hadagli as PW1 to 8 and marked Ex.P1 to 8.
10.

PW1 being the informant deposed in his evidence that, he was working as Chief Manager in the Bank of Baroda from 2006 to 2008, the accused has tendered the application for housing loan of Rs.6,45,000/- in April-2006 and produced salary slip for the month of March-2006 purported to be issued by AG's office.

A few months later, as the accused did not pay the loan installments, when he inquired at the office where she works, they informed in writing that they did not issue the alleged salary certificate and that she was not working under them at that time.
Thereafter, he filed complaint before police as per Ex.P1 and after receiving complaint the police have drawn mahazar as per Ex.P26 and he identified the documents as per Ex.P2 to 25.

11. PW2 being the Senior Manager of Bank and mahazar witness has admitted the signature in the Ex.P26 i.e. spot mahazar and he deposed he does not know the contents of the Ex.P26 and also the boundaries of the spot.

3 12.

sentences.text: PW3 to PW6 are being the officials of the Bank of Baroda, they deposed about the alleged incident and also issuance of Ex.P27 to 29 documents to the police.

PW7 and 8 are police officials,
who have deposed about the investigation of the case.
The learned counsel for the accused denied the evidence of PW2 to PW8 as false in the cross examination.

13. On perusal of oral as well as documentary evidence available on record, it is found that as per the prosecution the accused had intentionally produced fake salary certificate and also get loan to purchase the property.
But, on perusal of entire documentary evidence, the prosecution has not produced original salary slip.
On perusal of Ex.P3 i.e. copy of salary slip wherein the seal and signature of the drawing officer is not found.
In the offence relating to cheating, the prosecution must prove the dishonest intention of the accused to commit loss to any person.
But, the original salary certificate which is said to have produced by the accused at the time of granting loan stating that genuine pay slip is not produced before the court.
14. The prosecution has not given any explanation about what prevented them to produce original salary certificate which is said to have produced by the accused.
Moreover, in order to prove the case of the prosecution, after examination of chief of PW1, he has not stepped into the witness box to testify his evidence.
Hence, his evidence not cross examined by accused as he was not available for cross examination.
15. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence, it is found that the accused was working at AG's office, which is not disputed by prosecution.
As per the prosecution, the loan availed to the accused in the month of April-2006, the complaint was lodged on 01-05-2008 after lapse of 2 years.
Further more, on perusal of the documents before granting loan, the bank obtained legal opinion in respect of the property and also to grant the loan to the accused.
As per the valuation of the residential flat which is purchased by the accused for a sum of Rs.6,87,000/-.

Moreover, on perusal of copy of mortgage deed it is noticed that, at the time of purchasing property the accused had deposited original Sale Deed and other original documents pertaining to the purchased property.
16. As per the prosecution the accused dishonestly produced the fake salary certificate and availed loan.
If the accused had dishonest intention definitely she would had not deposit the original documents in the said bank.
Furthermore, the prosecution has not stated how much of amount due from the accused.
The prosecution has also not explained how the salary certificate was accepted without verifying the seal and signature of the drawing officer of the accused at the time of granting loan.

17. On perusal of evidence of PW1 who is the informant in the case, his evidence not testified by the accused as he was not available for cross examination, hence his evidence has no any evidentiary value.
The ingredients of alleged offences are not applicable to the present set of facts of the case.
Therefore, looking to the material placed on record, the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the offences alleged against above accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, as per the settled principles of law, the accused is entitled for benefit of doubt.
So by extending the benefit of doubt to accused, I answer the above points in the negative.

4 18. Point No.3:-

For the foregoing discussion and my findings to the above points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.420, 465, 468 of IPC by acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C.
In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C her bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six) months.
